main_text.head: Benevolo ac Candido LECTORI, ANTONIUS DEUSINGIUS Ϋγαίνειν.
main_text.p: Ira superstitionis vis est, Candide Lector, in animis mortalium superstitioni indulgentium: ut vel eveniat illis idipsum quod metuunt, inducente Numine supremo ea mala quae ipsi formidant, ut est apud Jef. 66. v. 3. 4. quia non respondent Deo vocanti per Scripturam ad media divina congrua voluntati ac jussui, nec auscultant Deo loquenti per Naturam, mediaque per eandem licita suggerenti: Sic vero id ipsum quod improbum timebat evenit ei, ut loquitur Sapiens Proverb. 10. v. 24. Vel obtingant iisdem, dum superstitionibus indulgent, ea bona quae exspectant, eventusque fortiantur superstitiosi speratos, cooperante Cacodaemone atque animos eorundem impietatibus implicante; justo interim Dei judicio permittente ut in errores delap

page.notes: The woodcut initial M is joined to "Ira"; the first word "Ira" reads as the opening of the paragraph. The line ending "dela-" is partly obscured; the final word is read as "delapsi" with doubt. Marks "* 4." below the last line are printer's marks and are not transcribed as text.
